author: Emma Lazarus
title: The Poems of Emma Lazarus, Volume I: Narrative, Lyric, and Dramatic
edition: Boston and New York: Houghton, Mifflin and Company, 1889. Scan-backed Wikisource page transcriptions, checked against downloaded images of every selected page. Identified transcription errors are corrected to the printed scan and logged. Page headers and the Colossus footnote marker/note are excluded; verse overflow and split words at physical line ends are rejoined to their poetic lines. Original wording and stanza structure retained. The library text holds pages 40-221 of the volume (the EPOCHS sequence, the narrative poems and the lyrics through RESTLESSNESS., with Lazarus's notes) as Wikisource transcribes them; the biographical sketch by another hand and The Spagnoletto are not held. For a calendar reading on 2026-11-18, HEROES. (scan pages 69-72, printed pages 55-58) was checked line by line against the downloaded page images and six dropped apostrophes and dashes were restored to the print.

rights.basis: The identified 1889 printed edition, including these original-English poems, was published before 1931 and its US term has expired. The linked scan-backed source reproduces the 1889 title and 1888 copyright pages. Modern site commentary is excluded.

A scratch converter drops each page's noinclude header and footer (running heads) and section tags; expands the formatting templates to their text (centring, sizes, small capitals, blocks, hanging indents, the floating and apostrophe quote templates; gaps as spaces; rules, line-break and spacing templates dropped; a row-of-asterisks template kept as a paragraph of asterisks); turns wiki links into their text and removes image links, italic and bold quote marks; closes block templates opened in one page and closed in the next page's header or footer and drops a stray < after one line break on scan page 200. Centred lines are headings (level 2); prose is paragraphs with line breaks joined by spaces; lines ended by line breaks form stanzas split at empty lines, a stanza or paragraph running on from one page to the next being rejoined unless the page ends with a blank line or nop. The three printed notes (ref tags) keep numbered references [1] to [3] at the place of the tag, and each note follows, as [Footnote n: text], the block in which its page ends. scope.note: Holds the narrative and lyric poems of volume I (scan pages 54-235, printed pages 40-221). Not held: the anonymous Biographical Sketch (front matter by another hand), and The Spagnoletto (scan pages 236-356), whose Wikisource pages were unproofread OCR at retrieval (stray braces, misread words) and could not be converted faithfully.
